Putting identity identifications into the inputs

The remark following horizontal compatibility says that the individual whiskering laws follow by taking some inputs to be identity identifications. There are endpoint comparisons in this substitution: inserting an identity identification produces whiskering, while inserting an identity functor changes the endpoints by a unitor. We display the resulting laws here.

We use the structures and coherences of Sections 1.1–1.2. Write \(\tau \cdot \sigma \) for vertical composition, \(u\star \sigma \) and \(\sigma \star k\) for whiskering, and \(\tau \ast \sigma \) for horizontal composition. The right-hand identification in a vertical composite is applied first. These operations also apply to families with a common parameter category \(X\), namely functors from \(X\) into fixed identification animae. For an absolute identification \(\delta \), write \(\overline \delta \) for its constant family on \(X\).

Supplementary Lemma 1. For \(f,f'\colon C\to D\), \(g,g'\colon D\to E\), and families \(\sigma \colon X\to (f=f')\) and \(\tau \colon X\to (g=g')\), there are identifications \[ \overline {\mathrm {id}_g}\ast \sigma =g\star \sigma , \qquad \tau \ast \overline {\mathrm {id}_f}=\tau \star f. \] In particular, \[ \overline {\mathrm {id}_g}\ast \overline {\mathrm {id}_f} =\overline {\mathrm {id}_{g\circ f}}. \]

Proof idea

By definition, \[ \tau \ast \sigma =(\tau \star f')\cdot (g\star \sigma ). \] If \(\tau \) is the constant identity family, preservation of identities by prewhiskering identifies the first factor with the constant identity of \(g\circ f'\). Apply the left vertical unit law. For the second formula, use preservation of identities by postwhiskering and the right vertical unit law. Constant families are compared with their whiskerings using the associator. Combining the first formula with preservation of identities by postwhiskering gives the last formula. □

The five endpoint-compatible laws

We use the book’s names for the structural identifications: \[ \lambda _f\colon \mathrm {id}\circ f=f,\qquad \rho _f\colon f\circ \mathrm {id}=f,\qquad \alpha _{f,g,h}\colon (h\circ g)\circ f=h\circ (g\circ f). \]

Supplementary Lemma 2. Let \(f,g\colon C\to D\) and put \(X=(f=g)\), with universal family \(\sigma =\mathrm {id}_{(f=g)}\). The unit comparisons give \[ \overline {\lambda _g}\cdot (\mathrm {id}_D\star \sigma ) =\sigma \cdot \overline {\lambda _f}, \qquad \overline {\rho _g}\cdot (\sigma \star \mathrm {id}_C) =\sigma \cdot \overline {\rho _f}. \] For \(u\colon D\to E\) and \(v\colon E\to F\), there is an identification \[ \overline {\alpha _{g,u,v}}\cdot ((v\circ u)\star \sigma ) =\bigl (v\star (u\star \sigma )\bigr )\cdot \overline {\alpha _{f,u,v}}. \] For \(k\colon B\to C\) and \(l\colon A\to B\), there is an identification \[ \overline {\alpha _{l,k,g}}\cdot ((\sigma \star k)\star l) =(\sigma \star (k\circ l))\cdot \overline {\alpha _{l,k,f}}. \] Finally, for \(k\colon B\to C\) and \(u\colon D\to E\), there is an identification \[ \overline {\alpha _{k,g,u}}\cdot ((u\star \sigma )\star k) =(u\star (\sigma \star k))\cdot \overline {\alpha _{k,f,u}}. \] All five are identifications between functors on \((f=g)\).

Proof idea

For the unit formulas, start with the horizontal unit comparisons and use Supplementary Lemma 1 to replace horizontal composition with an identity identification by whiskering.

For the postcomposition formula, substitute \(\overline {\mathrm {id}_v},\overline {\mathrm {id}_u},\sigma \) into horizontal associativity. The two parenthesizations become whiskering by \(v\circ u\) and successive whiskering by \(u\) and \(v\). The two vertical sides remain \(\overline {\alpha _{f,u,v}}\) and \(\overline {\alpha _{g,u,v}}\). The other two formulas use, respectively, \(\sigma ,\overline {\mathrm {id}_k},\overline {\mathrm {id}_l}\) and \(\overline {\mathrm {id}_u},\sigma ,\overline {\mathrm {id}_k}\). In each case the horizontal identity comparisons give the displayed boundary. □

Precomposing these universal comparisons with a family \(R\to (f=g)\) gives the corresponding formulas for that family. The endpoint normalizations are the ones explained in Specializing coherence laws. This derivation uses horizontal units and associativity together with the vertical laws and preservation of identity identifications by whiskering. It does not require interchange.

The middle interchange in a composite

The book also observes that horizontal composition preserves vertical composition. The following calculation makes explicit the single interchange needed for absolute identifications.

Supplementary Lemma 3. Let \(f_0,f_1,f_2\colon C\to D\) and \(g_0,g_1,g_2\colon D\to E\). For absolute identifications \(\sigma _i\colon f_{i-1}=f_i\) and \(\tau _i\colon g_{i-1}=g_i\), for \(i=1,2\), there is an identification \[ (\tau _2\cdot \tau _1)\ast (\sigma _2\cdot \sigma _1) =(\tau _2\ast \sigma _2)\cdot (\tau _1\ast \sigma _1). \] Horizontal composition also preserves identity identifications: \(\mathrm {id}_g\ast \mathrm {id}_f=\mathrm {id}_{g\circ f}\).

Proof idea

Expand the horizontal composite on the left and use preservation of vertical composition by each whiskering. This gives the four factors, in their order of vertical composition, \[ (\tau _2\star f_2),\quad (\tau _1\star f_2),\quad (g_0\star \sigma _2),\quad (g_0\star \sigma _1). \] The fixed-outer interchange comparison for \(\tau _1\), specialized at \(\sigma _2\), identifies the middle composite with \[ (\tau _1\star f_2)\cdot (g_0\star \sigma _2) =(g_1\star \sigma _2)\cdot (\tau _1\star f_1). \] Reassociate the four factors before and after this replacement. The result is exactly the right-hand horizontal composite. Preservation of identities follows by expanding its two whiskerings and then applying a vertical unit law. □

Here the inputs \(\tau _i,\sigma _i\) are absolute identifications. The proof uses the stated fixed-input interchange axiom. A comparison over a parameter category in which both interchange inputs vary is a stronger assertion; the formalization treats that assertion separately under an additional joint interchange hypothesis. The displayed result does not use that hypothesis.
